summary: WebSocket-driven remote shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade backdoor on installer host
details: On startup, the agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server (SERVER_URL) and routes inbound messages to handlers that grant the remote peer full control of the installer's host. terminal_create spawns an interactive PTY (bash/pwsh/cmd) via node-pty and terminal_input forwards server-supplied bytes directly to term.pty.write, yielding shell RCE driven by the WebSocket peer. The message router additionally exposes read_file, write_file, create_file, delete_files, move_files, copy_files, upload_to_dir, git_add/reset/restore/commit/push, and proxy_request handlers, giving the peer arbitrary filesystem, git, and HTTP-proxy access on the host. An upgrade_agent handler shells out to run `npm install -g @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` in a detached script and restarts the service, letting the server force the host to pull and execute new package versions on demand. service/linux.js modifies PATH via shell RC (`~/.local/bin:~/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`) to make the agent's CLI resolvable, supporting persistence of the launcher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
